pillarsModal.title: What goes into your score
pillarsModal.introLead: We learn how water usually behaves in
pillarsModal.introTrail: building, compare new behavior to that history, and to ideal benchmarks for how the whole system should behave. The index blends four kinds of signal—each one uses sensor data you already have on the main line.

p1.rest: — whether usage patterns, timing, and flow duration still match what we've learned is normal for you—new or drifting behavior gets flagged.

p2.rest: — how hard and how long the system is working versus its usual load (quick spikes vs sustained strain add up differently).

p3.rest: — whether toilets, dishwashers, and other draws still match their typical “signatures”; drift can mean wear or inefficiency before an obvious failure.

p4.rest: — vibration from the same sensor: turbulence and instability that don't line up with normal flow can point to strain in the plumbing system.

pillarsModal.footnote: Exact weighting stays tuned as we ship; the app will always show what drove a given score.

caseStudy.metaDescription: How a pipe burst and a rough prototype led to Beluga — real-time flow data, a 700 L/h anomaly, and why early water detection matters for Canadian buildings.
caseStudy.heroTitle: How a single pipe burst turned into a national problem worth solving

spark.title: The spark
spark.p1: The idea behind our system did not start in a lab or a pitch deck. It started with a phone call.
spark.p2: After hearing that our landlord had experienced a pipe burst in one of his buildings, we started asking a simple question: how often does this actually happen? What we found was alarming. In Canada, nearly 48 percent of home insurance claims are caused by water damage — almost double the rate seen in the United States. Yet most buildings still rely on noticing damage after it has already occurred.
spark.p3: We believed this was a problem worth solving.

prototype.title: The first prototype
prototype.p1: We moved fast. Within days, we built a rough, clunky first prototype. It was far from pretty, but it worked. The goal was simple: measure flow, establish a baseline, and see if early anomalies could be detected before damage occurred.
prototype.caption: Initial prototype installed and running

calibration.title: Calibration and the unexpected
calibration.p1: During the first two hours of testing, we focused on calibration and baseline measurements. Normal building usage - Toilets, sinks, background flow. Everything looked stable.
calibration.highlight: The system detected a sudden spike in flow: 700 liters per hour.
calibration.p3: At first, we assumed it was an error.
calibration.imgAlt: System alert showing a 700 L/h flow anomaly
calibration.caption: System alert showing a 700 L/h flow anomaly

findingSource.title: Finding the source
findingSource.p1: We searched the entire building, floor by floor, unit by unit. Eventually, we found the culprit. A hose connection had failed, likely due to pressure buildup, causing a massive and continuous leak.
findingSource.p2: Left undetected, this would have resulted in extensive water damage.
findingSource.imgAlt: Physical source of the leak identified on site
findingSource.caption: Physical source of the leak identified on site

validation.title: Real world validation
validation.p1: Our landlord and two building managers came on site immediately. Seeing the live flow data in real time changed the conversation. At that rate of water loss, the concern was no longer hypothetical. It was urgent.
validation.p2: They suspected the hose cap had blown off due to pressure. The main valve was shut off, and a full investigation began.
validation.imgAlt: Landlord and building managers inspecting the issue
validation.caption: Landlord and building managers inspecting the issue

mitigation.title: Mitigation confirmed
mitigation.p1: Once the main valve was closed, the system told the story instantly. Flow dropped to zero.
mitigation.imgAlt: Flow rate at zero confirming resolution
mitigation.caption: Flow rate at zero — issue fully resolved

whyMattered.title: Why this mattered
whyMattered.p1: This felt like more than coincidence.
whyMattered.p2: Within hours of installing a rough prototype, it had already prevented what could have been a costly and damaging incident. That moment made something very clear to us: this was not an edge case. This was a systemic problem across Canadian buildings.
whyMattered.p3: From a founder's perspective, this was the turning point. We were no longer experimenting with an idea. We were staring at a real, measurable problem that affects homeowners, landlords, insurers, and cities across Canada.
whyMattered.p4: And it was clear that early detection, not cleanup, is the solution.
whyMattered.p5: This case study became the foundation for everything we are building next.

support.metaDescription: Contact Beluga for help with your sensor, dashboard, or troubleshooting. Email and phone support.
support.title: Support
support.intro: Need help with Beluga? We're here for you. Whether you have a question about your sensor, need help reading your dashboard, or want to report an issue — our team is happy to assist.
support.contactBody: The fastest way to reach us is by email. Send us a message and we'll get back to you within one business day. You can also call if you prefer to talk through an issue.
support.q1: How do I install the sensor?
support.a1: Beluga clamps onto the outside of your pipe — no cutting, no plumber needed. It works on copper, PEX, CPVC, and galvanized pipes.
support.a2: Not at the pipe. The sensor transmits data via LoRa to a hub elsewhere in the building that has connectivity.
support.q3: How do I read my dashboard?
support.a3: The app shows real-time flow in litres per hour, historical usage charts, and alert notifications. If something looks off, the app will tell you what it means and what to do.
support.q4: I think my sensor is offline
support.a4: Check that the hub has power and connectivity. If the issue persists, email us and we'll troubleshoot it with you.

hero.subtitle: Beluga estimates directional plumbing risk from an address using public records, infrastructure heuristics, and regional water-system signals. To learn more about your property and get accurate real-time data, you'll need a Beluga device.
hero.searchHint: Try a full street address. Estimates work best for the United States and Canada.

confidence.tooltip: Confidence reflects how much public and infrastructure signal we could match to this address.

results.categoriesSubtitle: 1 = highest risk · 10 = strongest signals for health

narrative.excellent: Signals line up positively across the board. If a real assessment confirms these, this property looks well-maintained and low-risk from a plumbing perspective.
narrative.good: Most indicators are healthy with a few mild watch points. A Beluga assessment can confirm which categories deserve attention first.
narrative.watch: Several categories show elevated risk signals. A real assessment is worthwhile to turn these directional reads into confirmed findings.
narrative.action: Multiple categories are signalling meaningful risk. We'd strongly recommend a real plumbing intelligence assessment to validate and prioritize.

rationale.default: Estimated from building era, local infrastructure age, and available address signals.
rationale.preWar: Pre-war building era — supply lines and service laterals have likely aged past prime.
rationale.midCentury: Mid-century era — mixed galvanized and early copper still common in service.
rationale.modern: Modern-era supply infrastructure typical for this area.
rationale.recent: Recent-build supply lines — well within expected service life.
rationale.agingMains: Regional water mains skew old — baseline pipe-condition risk is elevated.
rationale.modernMains: Region has relatively modern water mains — lower baseline risk.
rationale.coastalExposure: Coastal air and brackish groundwater accelerate supply-line corrosion.
rationale.floodExposure: Historic flood exposure stresses buried supply lines over time.
rationale.hardWater: Regional hard water accelerates scale buildup in older supply piping.

rationale.default: Combines pipe-age priors with regional climate stress signals.
rationale.freezeThaw: Freeze-thaw climate elevates joint fatigue and pinhole failures in aging lines.
rationale.preWar: Pre-war service lines carry above-average leak probability under load.
rationale.midCentury: Mid-century era — fittings and valves are nearing end of reliable service life.
rationale.modern: Modern-era lines keep baseline leak probability low.
rationale.recent: Recent builds — modern PEX or copper keeps leak probability very low.
rationale.agingMains: Aging municipal mains feed this area — more breaks upstream of the service line.
rationale.combinedSewer: Combined-sewer backups can pressurise lines adversely during storms.
rationale.modernMains: Relatively modern mains in this area — lower failure rates expected.

rationale.default: Reflects municipal supply and building stack priors.
rationale.denseUrban: Dense urban stacks see pressure swings across floors — elevated irregularity risk.
rationale.urbanCore: Urban-core supply patterns add moderate pressure variability.
rationale.commercialUse: Commercial fixture loads and backflow devices add pressure-irregularity risk.
rationale.residentialUse: Residential supply profile — pressure irregularities uncommon.
rationale.freezeThaw: Freeze-thaw cycles periodically disrupt main pressure in this region.
rationale.agingMains: Aging mains carry higher likelihood of pressure irregularities.
rationale.modernMains: Modern mains in this area support stable delivered pressure.
rationale.preWar: Pre-war building stacks often have uneven pressure across units.
rationale.recent: Modern stacks and pressure-balancing — stable delivered pressure expected.

rationale.default: Reflects water chemistry, install era, and usage profile.
rationale.hardWater: Regional hard water shortens cartridge, valve, and flush-mechanism lifespans.
rationale.preWar: Pre-war era fixtures have typically been replaced, but risers often remain original.
rationale.midCentury: Mid-century fixtures — seals and valve cartridges approaching end of life.
rationale.modern: Modern-era fixtures — normal wear profile expected.
rationale.recent: Recent-build fixtures — early-life wear profile only.
rationale.commercialUse: High-use commercial fixtures accelerate wear and seal failures.
rationale.residentialUse: Residential usage — normal fixture wear expected.
rationale.coastalExposure: Coastal air accelerates finish and cartridge corrosion.

rationale.default: Area-level drainage and sewer context may create moderate backup risk.
rationale.combinedSewer: Combined-sewer service area — backup and surcharge risk is historically elevated.
rationale.floodExposure: Historic flood and stormwater exposure raises drainage-backup probability.
rationale.coastalExposure: Coastal / high-water-table conditions elevate infiltration and root intrusion.
rationale.preWar: Era-appropriate clay or cast-iron laterals carry higher cracking and intrusion risk.
rationale.midCentury: Mid-century laterals are approaching typical replacement age.
rationale.modern: Modern PVC drainage typical for this area — baseline risk only.
rationale.recent: Recent-build PVC drainage — baseline risk is low.
rationale.urbanCore: Dense urban drainage networks carry modestly higher surcharge risk.

rationale.default: Blends fixture-era priors with regional usage and climate pressure.
rationale.droughtExposed: Drought-exposed region combined with older fixtures — waste risk is meaningful.
rationale.droughtEfficient: Drought-exposed region with modern fixtures — efficiency strongly supported.
rationale.hardWater: Hard water reduces fixture efficiency over time as scale accumulates.
rationale.commercialUse: Commercial usage patterns with legacy fixtures carry higher waste risk.
rationale.residentialUse: Residential usage profile — moderate, stable waste risk expected.
rationale.preWar: Pre-war installed fixtures use well above modern efficiency standards.
rationale.midCentury: Mid-century fixtures — noticeably less efficient than modern equivalents.
rationale.recent: Recent-build fixtures — strong efficiency baselines throughout.

rationale.default: Reflects how much signal we could match to this address.
rationale.richSignals: Strong address match with multiple public data signals.
rationale.goodCoverage: Good regional coverage and a clean address match.
rationale.partialCoverage: Partial coverage — street-level match with moderate regional signal density.
rationale.areaOnly: Only area-level data matched — rescore with a full street address for higher confidence.
rationale.limitedRegion: Region sits outside our strongest coverage footprint — signals are thinner than typical.

why.title: Why this score?
why.intro: This estimate blends regional infrastructure priors, building-age heuristics, and environmental signals resolved from the address. It is deliberately explainable — nothing is a black box.

disclaimer.title: Estimated, not inspected
disclaimer.body: This score is an estimate based on location, property signals, and infrastructure heuristics. It is not a substitute for physical inspection or licensed evaluation.

howItWorks.title: From an address to a directional plumbing read.
howItWorks.subtitle: Three deterministic steps. No black-box models — every score is traceable to the signals that produced it.

ingest.title: Ingest address signals
ingest.body: We resolve the address into region, property type, postal code, and building-stock era — the backbone of every downstream estimate.

heuristics.title: Apply infrastructure heuristics
heuristics.body: Regional priors for pipe age, sewer topology, water chemistry, and climate shape each category's baseline risk.

estimate.title: Produce an explainable score
estimate.body: Seven category scores roll up into one overall read, each with a rationale and a confidence signal for transparency.

trust.title: Built to be inspected, not trusted blindly.
trust.body: Every score is signal-based and directional. Categories are weighted for decision-making, not marketing. Today's estimate runs on public and regional data; tomorrow's will layer in Beluga's live infrastructure network.
trust.note: Same address, same score — deterministic by design, so you can compare and defend numbers over time.

permits.title: Permit and construction records
permits.body: Local permit histories and construction era data feed pipe-age and fixture-wear priors.

buildingAge.title: Building-age datasets
buildingAge.body: Parcel-level age data calibrates per-address risk against regional building-stock distributions.

environmental.title: Environmental and climate data
environmental.body: Freeze-thaw exposure, drought stress, and coastal proximity inform leak and drainage risk.

belugaNetwork.title: Beluga infrastructure network
belugaNetwork.body: Real-world fixture behaviour from the Beluga sensor network will progressively replace heuristics with measured signal.

finalCta.title: Turn a directional estimate into a confirmed assessment.
